subject: HydraSys QA simulation — ops plan, scripts, IP allowlist and test window
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@hydrasys.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>; marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyanka Sinha <prianka@hydrasys.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: QA simulation — initial details and ask

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap from my side and the items we need to lock down before our customer-led run: 

1) Success criteria (what we need to validate):
   - 95th percentile latency under 350ms for single-shot gen (seq len ~ 256)
   - Sustained throughput of 180 tokens/sec aggregate across the cluster for peak window
   - Streaming session concurrency target: 160 concurrent streaming sessions with max 200 kb/s per session

2) Test approach: HydraOps will run a k6-based scenario that simulates our front-end batching and streaming client behavior. We plan two phases: a smoke run (15m) then a full 90-minute window.

3) Required from Redwood:
   - A test account with explicit rate limits matching production (or a dedicated slot)
   - IPs to add to HydraSys allowlist (we will supply exact CIDRs)
   - Any runbook/checklist you recommend for graceful fallback if latency spikes

I attached the draft k6 script (hydrasys_k6_script_v1.js) — it includes both single-shot and streaming probes. Priyanka will follow up with exact source IP ranges by EOD.

Next steps: please confirm available test windows (preferably next Tue/Wed morning PT), and whether you can provide a dedicated test slot or guidance for safe load against staging.

Thanks — Rajesh
---
Rajesh Kumar
Head of QA Automation, HydraSys
rajesh@hydrasys.ai
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@hydrasys.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>; neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QA simulation — initial details and ask

Thanks Rajesh — this is clear and a good framing. A few clarifying points from Redwood's side and what we'll prepare ahead of the run:

- Test account: we can provision a dedicated test consumer key with per-minute quotas identical to your target profile. That will isolate your run from other customers.
- IP allowlist: please send the CIDR list into ops+qa@redwood.ai; our networking team will prioritize same-day add for /24 and smaller ranges.
- Streaming: our streaming path is optimized for 64k chunk windows. For 200 kb/s per session we'll need to confirm the chunking on your client.

Runbook items we'll send (attached as redwood_runbook_v1.pdf):
  * Pre-run checklist (token limits, model variant pinning, cold-warm cache state)
  * During-run monitoring dashboard links and sodium alerts we recommend
  * Fallback play: automatic revert to smaller model variant + traffic shedding on 95th latency > 450ms for 5m

Available windows: Tue 2028-05-16 10:00–12:00 PT and Wed 2028-05-17 09:00–11:30 PT. If neither works, we can open a short window on Mon 2028-05-15 afternoon.

We'll also run a short internal smoke with our SEs on Mon morning to validate the k6 script includes realistic streaming client hooks. Can you confirm the streaming protocol (SSE vs WebSocket) your client uses?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@hydrasys.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>; aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyanka Sinha <prianka@hydrasys.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QA simulation — initial details and ask

Marissa — good list. Answers below: 

- Streaming protocol: our client uses WebSocket with a small keepalive ping every 30s. Payloads are framed so bandwidth per session peaks around 160–210 kb/s depending on token density.
- We'll send CIDRs in a CSV (attached as ip_allowlist_requests.csv) — those are the test runner IPs and our CI agents.
- For the k6 script: the v1 file includes a pseudo-WebSocket adapter; we can convert to a Locust task if you prefer. HydraOps favors k6 for CI integration.

We can take Tue 2028-05-16 10:00–12:00 PT for the full run. Please provision the test account and confirm the slot. Also please share the dashboard URL and the escalation contact for on-call infra during the window.

Thanks — Rajesh
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@hydrasys.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>; neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2028 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QA simulation — initial details and ask

Rajesh — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. Confirmations below and one small ask:

Confirmed actions from Redwood:
- Dedicated test API key: HYDRA-DH4721-T1 (scope: test-only, rate-limited to match requested profile). I will DM credentials to Rajesh and Priyanka and also publish temporary creds in our shared run link.
- IP allowlist: piccced ops@redwood.ai and they will apply the CSV you attached. Expect completion by Mon 17:00 PT.
- Dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/run/DH-4721 (real-time token/latency breakdown + per-connection traces).
- On-call escalation: neha_kapoor (pager: +1-415-555-0199) will be primary during the window; Marissa will coordinate the SE side.

A couple operational notes:
- Cache-warm strategy: please run a 10-minute warm-up at 30% traffic before the full window to populate KV caches and avoid cold-start tail latency.
- If you need to convert k6 WebSocket adapter to Locust, Marissa can work with your engineers on a quick mapping.

I'll queue the key and ops tickets now and share confirmation by EOD. Confirm RX: you and Priyanka got the time slot?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
From: Priyanka Sinha <prianka@hydrasys.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>; marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@hydrasys.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2028 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QA simulation — initial details and ask

Thanks Aditya — we received the slot and the brief. Quick confirmations from HydraSys ops: 

- Slot accepted: Tue 2028-05-16 10:00–12:00 PT.
- CIDRs submitted (file: ip_allowlist_requests.csv) — please confirm when rules are live.
- We'll run the warm-up you recommended (10m at 30%).
- Attachment note: hydrasys_k6_script_v1.js contains two scenarios — single_shot.js and streaming_emulation.js. We will run the smoke (single_shot) at 09:40 PT and begin the warm-up at 09:50 PT.

If you can send the test API key by EOD that would be great. Also, can you add a short run note in the dashboard with the run id DH-4721-T1 so we can correlate logs on our side?

Best,
Priyanka Sinha
QA Automation Lead, HydraSys
